title: Design the portable command control-plane adapter
description: Map the additive control-plane schema, dispatch routing, lifecycle mutations, structured command conversion, and migration boundaries required to connect the portable worker without disrupting the legacy Celery path. Produce an evidence-backed design and unresolved decisions only; do not edit source code or infrastructure.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Read-only investigation started in parallel with the drainable service implementation. It is mapping additive task lifecycle fields, atomic mutation requirements, structured command seams, generic routing options, stream-dispatch isolation, and a safe parallel migration sequence. No source or external state changes are authorized.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text:
## Investigation result

Verified migration constraints:
- The Task record is both the dashboard lifecycle contract and the legacy Celery stream trigger.
- Any inserted Task with dispatchStatus PENDING currently reaches Celery unless metadata marks one of two self-managed modes.
- Portable routing and the complete envelope must therefore be pinned on the initial create; a two-phase update is unsafe.
- The legacy dispatcher deny guard must deploy before any portable producer.
- Raw GraphQL model mutations support conditions, but existing Task helpers do not expose them.
- Direct DynamoDB lifecycle writes would bypass current AppSync mutation subscriptions.
- Current Task API authorization does not provide a ready ECS workload-identity path.
- Typed command inputs exist before string rendering for most command families; arbitrary command input remains an explicit legacy case.

Recommended migration sequence for main-agent planning:
1. Add nullable route and lifecycle fields.
2. Add and test a fail-closed legacy dispatcher route guard while absent route remains legacy.
3. Introduce one typed portable producer and a conditional lifecycle adapter in development.
4. Prove duplicate, recovery, stale completion, cancellation, dead-letter, and subscription behavior.
5. Route new production Tasks through an explicit generic policy while in-flight routes remain immutable.

Evidence was independently verified at the active dispatcher, Amplify Task schema/auth, conditional mutation example, Python Task helper, and subscription selections. No source or external state was changed.
